weaknesses.summary: 17/20 agents flagged this — hidden guardrail risk.

The conversion metric is positive and separable (+7.5pp), but sentiment is negative and separable (-13.3) across the paired arms — the metric would greenlight a change users dislike. Pre-calibration (#222), trust sentiment for harm: do not ship on the metric alone.

refinement_suggestions: Narrow the test cohort to single-active-series viewers (users with exactly one in-progress series and no in-progress movies in the past 14 days), where the algorithm's 'most likely title' prediction is near-deterministic and the hidden-guardrail risk of surfacing the wrong title is minimized. Exclude multi-show jugglers entirely from this experiment phase.

Add a persistent, visible 'Switch title' affordance directly on the Smart Resume hero card (not buried in a 'More options' expander) so users who disagree with the algorithmic pick can correct it in one tap without losing the fast-resume benefit. Measure both resume-button CTR and 'Switch title' usage rate as co-primary metrics to detect cases where the mechanism is failing to predict correctly.

Gate the ship decision on a composite success criterion that requires BOTH a statistically significant lift in resume-session starts (the conversion metric) AND a neutral-or-positive net sentiment score from in-app post-session micro-surveys ('Did the app make it easy to get back to your show?'), explicitly preventing the positive conversion metric from greenlighting the feature while sentiment remains negative.

result_full.metric_lift_relative: Treatment converts directionally higher than control on 20 paired identities; the paired-bootstrap interval excludes zero. Synthetic conversion is a weak behavioral signal — read as rank/direction, not as a calibrated effect size. NOTE: one or more personas in this run lack per-persona behavioral seeds (a v1.0-class pack), so cross-persona variance is degraded — a flat or non-separable metric here may reflect collapsed agent variance rather than a true null effect. Rebuild the pack to v1.1 to de-attenuate.
result_full.metric_sentiment_disagreement_caveat: Metric↔sentiment DISAGREEMENT (harm-misread): the conversion metric reads +7.5pp (CI [+4.0, +11.0]pp), positive and separable — it would greenlight this change — while sentiment is -13.3 (CI [-21.5, -4.6]), negative and separable. This can indicate real user harm the uncalibrated metric misses. Trust sentiment for harm until the metric is calibrated (#222).
